rationale: This is a denominator swap on the archive's Depreciation-Reserved Cash Value that mostly reproduces the published cash-flow-to-enterprise-value multiple, and the net-debt EV base it adopts can go negative for cash-rich firms — the opposite of the stability the reasoning claims.

Netting short-term debt from cash and switching from a multiplicative to a binding conditional structure is an economically motivated, sign-consistent modification of Cash-Composition Book Value, though it verges on a generic value-times-financial-strength double sort and will be highly correlated with the archived version.

Adding cash to the market-cap denominator of the archived Unfunded Inventory Build Yield is a cosmetic rescaling that will leave ranks nearly unchanged for most firms and does not address the diagnosed slope-versus-alpha disagreement.

The dollar-level MIN is only interpretable as "jointly present financing" when both terms are positive — in the long leg it conflates receivable collection with debt paydown — and the construct closely echoes the archived Short-Debt-Funded Accrual Trap with the numerator narrowed to receivables.

Converting the low-water-mark working-capital overhang from an effective-price adjustment into a separate binding hurdle is a structurally different, internally consistent response to the diagnosed weak-alpha problem, and the overhang measure itself is not a standard published accrual.

Dropping cash from the denominator makes this largely the well-known EBITDA-to-enterprise-value multiple, and the bolted-on penalty — a 3-observation volatility estimate scaled by assets — is too noisy and likely too small relative to EV to make the stated stability channel identifiable.
